newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania's president swears in new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania's president swears in new cabinet.

text.p: New members of Tanzania's cabinet were sworn in on Wednesday but diplomats were less than enthusiastic about the reshuffle except for the confirmation of Daniel Yona as finance minister.
The reshuffle was expected in the wake of the resignations of finance minister Simon Mbilinyi and natural resources and tourism minister Juma Ngasongwa.
President Benjamin Mkapa on Tuesday confirmed the December appointment of Yona and also gave him the planning portfolio.
"We're very pleased at the confirmation of minister Yona," World Bank representative Ron Brigish told Reuters on Wednesday.
But a diplomat said the other changes looked more like a technical reshuffle.
Another diplomat said he was disappointed that the cabinet had been enlarged through appointments of deputy ministers.

"This is not in line with what we understood we needed, a lean and clean government. It might be clean but it's not lean. I suspect the president has calculated this to consolidate his political position," he said.
Tanzanian opposition parties criticised the bigger cabinet, saying it was an additional burden on the tax-paying public.
Aaron Chiduo, a doctor, was appointed health minister and Nassoro Malocho, a deputy minister, was promoted to minister of state for planning and parastatal reform.

Mkapa transferred Health Minister Zakia Meghji to the ministry of natural resources and tourism while Industry and Trade Minister Abdallah Kigoda moved to energy and minerals where he swapped portfolios with William Shija.
Yona's confirmation was widely expected following his role in securing a decision last month by the Paris Club of creditor nations to give its most generous terms of debt reduction to Tanzania.
